lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1764 — a new storm, and two drawers that now start shut

Two owner instructions, unrelated, both small, arriving together.

1. THE COUNTER NOW OPENS WITH EVERY DRAWER SHUT
   Owner: *"workings to learn and reinforce your gear should start collapsed like
   the rest of the categories when it shops and vendors."*
   They were the only two sections on the vendor counter defaulting OPEN. The
   wares above them have opened collapsed since OTA-686, and so has the SELL
   tab's category list — measured, not assumed: four `collapsedSections[secKey]
   ?? …` sites, two `true` and two `false`, and the two `false` ones were exactly
   the two the owner named.
   ⚠ WORKINGS TO LEARN carried the note *"open by default — this is the
   discoverable bit"*. That was a real intention and it is OVERRIDDEN rather than
   quietly deleted: a section that opens itself while its neighbours stay shut
   does not read as discoverable, it reads as the odd one out, and it spends the
   first screen — the part the player came to the counter for — on something they
   did not ask to see. The count in the header already advertises it, which is
   the same job without costing the fold.
   ⚠⚠ THE TOGGLES MOVED TOO, AND THAT IS THE HALF THAT WOULD HAVE BITTEN. A
   header that RENDERS from `?? true` but TOGGLES from `!(s[key] ?? false)`
   writes `true` on the first tap — the section is already shut, so tapping it
   shuts it again and the control reads as dead. Both halves of both sections
   now read the same default, and a test asserts the toggles and the renders
   agree rather than just checking the renders.

2. ENVIRONMENTAL IS A THUNDERSTORM. L544 IS RETIRED.
   The trial's own first report said `L544` *"reads as a container / kit, not as
   an environment or a hazard. Its silhouette is a rectangle."* The owner reached
   the same verdict — *"it visually reads as a suitcase/case rather than an
   environmental hazard"* — and supplied a custom Tartaria thunderstorm.
   ⚠⚠⚠ AND NO CODE CHANGED, WHICH WAS THE ACTUAL TEST. Owner: *"So if the
   architecture is correct, this should require no UI behavior change."*
   It required none. `app/engine/damageIcons.ts` is untouched. The trial block is
   untouched. The semantic key, the mapping, the layout, the size experiment and
   live combat are all untouched. The diff for this half is one binary and two
   documents — because a correct art table means swapping a picture is swapping
   a FILE. A test asserts the table still says
   `environmental: require('../../assets/damage/environmental.png')`, that the
   word `L544` appears nowhere in it, and that no special case for one icon crept
   into the trial block.

   ⚠ THE MASTERS ARE TRACKED AND NOT BUNDLED, WHICH IS A REAL DISTINCTION HERE.
   `app.json` bundles `assets/**/*` into the app. Dropping 64/128/256/512 into
   `assets/damage/` would have shipped 750KB of one icon to a phone that only
   ever draws the 64. They go to `art/12-damage-icons/` instead — the drop-folder
   tree `art/README.md` already describes, tracked in git, invisible to the
   bundler. Owner: *"Do not load all four resolutions into the mobile runtime
   merely because they exist."*
   The runtime copy is proved md5-identical to the 64 master, so the two cannot
   silently drift into a stale export nobody can tell apart by looking, and a
   test walks all of `app/` to prove nothing `require()`s a master.

   PROVENANCE, recorded in `assets/damage/README.md` and `art/12-damage-icons/`:
     Source ................ Custom Tartaria Environmental Thunderstorm
     Asset family .......... custom
     Semantic filename ..... environmental.png (UNCHANGED)
     Master resolutions .... 64 / 128 / 256 / 512
     Runtime test .......... 64x64
     Status ................ PROVISIONAL, pending actual-device approval
     Retired ............... L544, no longer Environmental, kept nowhere

⚠⚠⚠ TWELVE TESTS FAILED ON THE COLLAPSE, ACROSS THREE SUITES, AND EVERY ONE WAS
THE CHANGE WORKING RATHER THAN A REGRESSION. `ota1734`, `ota1736` and `ota1740`
all drive the REINFORCE flow, and a row inside a shut drawer is not mounted at
all — so "find the Rusted Blade" found nothing. The fix is what a PLAYER now
does: the mount helpers tap the closed headers open. Not one assertion was
weakened; the flows still prove what they proved.
⚠⚠ AND THE FIRST FIX FOR IT WAS WRONG IN TWO WAYS AT ONCE, BOTH WORTH KEEPING:
  · `TouchableOpacity` is a COMPOSITE that forwards its props, so `findAll`
    returns the composite AND the host node for one control. Pressing every
    match toggled each header an EVEN number of times — open, then shut — and
    the render came back looking untouched, as if the taps had done nothing.
    Same trap OTA-1762's suite hit counting tabs. Deduped by rendered text.
  · `CONTRACTS ▸` carries a chevron IN ITS LABEL and is not a section header at
    all — it opens the mission board. Matching on the chevron alone tapped it
    and buried the counter under a modal, which is what the failure output
    actually showed before I read it properly.
`ota1736` already had a working `expandAll` that deduped by text; the two suites
that did not are the two that broke.

⚠ ONE OBSERVATION FOR THE OWNER, ACTED ON IN NO WAY: the replacement is a
full-bleed tile like seven of the others, where `L544` was one of three objects
on transparency. So the framed/unframed split this trial reported has narrowed
from 3-vs-6 to 2-vs-7 — `impact` and `rupture` are now the only two sitting on
the card ground. That is a consequence of the swap worth seeing before the set is
judged as a set, not a request to change anything.

Tests: __tests__/ota1764TheStormAndTheShutDrawers.test.tsx (12 tests) — all four
section defaults counted and proved to agree, which is a stronger claim than "the
two I changed are now true" and fails if a fifth is ever added open; ⚠ the
toggles proved to read the same default as the renders; the overridden
"discoverable bit" reasoning proved still present; the new binary proved 64x64
RGBA and proved NOT to be the rejected hash; ⚠⚠ the art table proved untouched
and free of `L544`; the masters proved tracked, correctly sized, outside the
bundled tree, byte-identical to the runtime copy at 64, and required by nothing
in `app/`.
⚠ That last one first failed on `buildInfo.ts` — the stamp ledger NAMES what each
pass did, so of course it says "12-damage-icons". Grading it would be grading the
write-up instead of the fix, which is the trap five checks in this rollout have
already hit, so it is excluded by name and the file count is asserted so the walk
cannot quietly find nothing.
⚠ And I first asserted THREE section defaults and forgot the SELL tab's, which is
the argument for counting them rather than listing the ones I touched.
